In node2vec, the 2nd-order random walk transition bias \u03b1_pq(t, x) depends on the graph distance between the previous node t and the candidate next node x, relative to the current node v. The walk chooses the next step from neighbors x of v with probability proportional to \u03b1_pq(t, x) \u00d7 w_vx, where w_vx is the edge weight.

The bias is defined by three cases:
- If x = t, then \u03b1_pq(t, x) = 1/p. This is the return move, so smaller p makes immediately going back to t more likely, while larger p suppresses backtracking.
- If x is adjacent to t, then \u03b1_pq(t, x) = 1. This is the neutral case.
- If x is not adjacent to t, then \u03b1_pq(t, x) = 1/q. This is the outward move, so smaller q makes exploration farther from t more likely, while larger q discourages moving outward.

Interpretation:
- p controls the likelihood of returning to the previous node, so it tunes backtracking versus forward progress.
- q controls the breadth-first versus depth-first tendency of the walk: q > 1 biases toward staying close to the current neighborhood, while q < 1 biases toward exploring nodes farther away from the previous node.

So, in short: p governs return behavior, and q governs exploration bias between local neighborhood sampling and outward exploration.
